Follows the PCSuite "Parameters Download" convention: reads the .par file, validates parameters against the connected controller, then sends each as a SET command. Ethernet connections use bulk messages (up to 50 per packet); other channels send one by one. After a successful download, optionally sends "ASave" plus per-axis "CalcFilters" to persist parameters to flash. The call is non-blocking; subscribe to the callbacks to be notified of progress and completion. public static void DownloadParameters(MotionController controller, string filePath, bool calcAndSave = true, Action<int> onProgress = null, Action<ParamHandlingSummary, string> onDone = null) Parameters controller MotionController Connected motion controller. filePath string Full path of the source .par file. calcAndSave bool If true (default), sends "ASave" + per-axis "CalcFilters" after download completes, persisting parameters to flash. Set to false to leave parameters in RAM only. onProgress Action<int> Optional callback invoked with progress percentage (0-100). onDone Action<ParamHandlingSummary, string> Optional callback invoked on completion. Argument 1 is a ParamHandlingSummary with statistics (null on early failure); argument 2 is an error description (empty string on success). Examples AAMotionAPI.DownloadParameters(controller, @"C:\Params\backup.par", calcAndSave: true, onProgress: pct => Console.WriteLine($"Download progress: {pct}%"), onDone: (summary, err) => { if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(err)) Console.WriteLine($"Download OK: {summary.SuccessCount}/{summary.TotalCount} parameters"); else Console.WriteLine($"Download failed: {err}"); }); Default: 1ms public static int FastReadCacheRefreshIntervalMs { get; set; } Property Value int FastReadEnabled Global switch to enable/disable fast read cache for all controllers. When true, reading Speed, Pos, MotionStat, InTargetStat etc. will read from a local cache that is refreshed every FastReadCacheRefreshIntervalMs milliseconds, instead of sending commands to the controller. This significantly reduces latency. Default: false (disabled for backward compatibility). public static bool FastReadEnabled { get; set; } Property Value bool Remarks Set to true before or after connecting to enable fast cached reads. The cache is automatically populated with common parameters (A/B/C axes) on connection. api/AAMotion.Extensions.html.title: Namespace AAMotion.Extensions | Agito AAMotion SDK
api/AAMotion.Extensions.html.summary: Namespace AAMotion.Extensions Classes AAMotionParametersDownload Asynchronously downloads (writes) controller parameters from a .par file. "Download" in this context follows the PCSuite convention: a local .par file's contents are written to the controller. Mirrors the PCSuite "Parameters Download" tool: reads the .par file, validates parameters against the connected controller, then sends each as a SET command. Ethernet connections use Bulk messages (up to 50 per packet); other channels send one by one. After successful download, optionally sends "Save" plus per-axis "CalcFilters" to persist parameters to flash. AAMotionParametersUpload Asynchronously uploads (saves) controller parameters to a .par file. "Upload" in this context follows the PCSuite convention: controller disk contents are read and persisted to a local file. Mirrors the PCSuite "Parameters Upload" tool: queries every supported parameter, writes them with header (product type, firmware/FPGA version, date, checksum) to a plain ASCII .par file. Ethernet connections use Bulk messages (up to 50 per packet); other channels send one by one. ParamHandlingSummary Summary of a parameter upload or download operation.

ECAM_CreateLinearTable(int, int, int, int, int) Create a simple ECAM table with linear interpolation between start and end positions. void ECAM_CreateLinearTable(int startPos, int endPos, int numPoints, int startIndex, int tableNum = 1) Parameters startPos int Starting position endPos int Ending position numPoints int Number of interpolation points startIndex int Start index in GenData array tableNum int ECAM table number (1-10, default: 1) Remarks This method automatically generates a linear ECAM table and stores it in the GenData array. The table will contain numPoints positions linearly interpolated between startPos and endPos. ECAM_CreateSinusoidalTable(int, int, int, int, int) Create a sinusoidal ECAM table. void ECAM_CreateSinusoidalTable(int amplitude, int offset, int numPoints, int startIndex, int tableNum = 1) Parameters amplitude int Sinusoidal amplitude offset int Position offset numPoints int Number of points in the table startIndex int Start index in GenData array tableNum int ECAM table number (1-10, default: 1) Remarks This method automatically generates a sinusoidal ECAM table and stores it in the GenData array. The table will contain numPoints positions following a sinusoidal pattern with specified amplitude and offset. ECAM_GetCycleCount(int) Get current ECAM cycle count for specified table. int ECAM_GetCycleCount(int tableNum = 1) Parameters tableNum int ECAM table number (1-10, default: 1) Returns int Current cycle count Remarks Returns the number of cycles completed for the specified ECAM table. ECAM_IsActive() Check if ECAM motion is currently active. bool ECAM_IsActive() Returns bool Returns true if ECAM motion is active, otherwise false. Remarks Use this method to monitor the status of ECAM motion during operation. ECAM_SetCycleParams(int, int, int, int) Set ECAM cycle parameters. void ECAM_SetCycleParams(int startCycIndex, int endCycIndex, int cycles, int tableNum = 1) Parameters startCycIndex int Start cycle index for repetition (0-based) endCycIndex int End cycle index for repetition (0-based) cycles int Number of cycles (positive for forward, negative for bidirectional, 2147483647 for infinite) tableNum int ECAM table number (1-10, default: 1) Remarks These parameters control how the ECAM table is repeated during motion. ECAM_SetGap(int, int) Set ECAM gap between master positions. void ECAM_SetGap(int gap, int tableNum = 1) Parameters gap int Gap between master positions (negative for reverse direction) tableNum int ECAM table number (1-10, default: 1) Remarks The gap determines the step size for master position increments during ECAM motion. Negative values reverse the direction of motion. ECAM_SetMaster(int, int) Set ECAM master axis (typically the main axis being followed). void ECAM_SetMaster(int masterKeyword, int tableNum = 1) Parameters masterKeyword int Master axis keyword code (e.g., 2 for PosRef, 24 for PosRef) tableNum int ECAM table number (1-10, default: 1) Remarks The master axis is the reference axis that the slave axis follows during ECAM motion. Common master keywords: 2 (PosRef), 24 (PosRef), etc. ECAM_SetMasterIni(int, int) Set ECAM master initial position compensation. void ECAM_SetMasterIni(int masterIni, int tableNum = 1) Parameters masterIni int Master initial position compensation value tableNum int ECAM table number (1-10, default: 1) Remarks This parameter compensates for the initial position difference between master and slave axes. ECAM_SetTableData(int[], int) Set ECAM table data using GenData array. Data will be written starting from ECAMStart[tableNum] to ECAMEnd[tableNum]. void ECAM_SetTableData(int[] data, int tableNum = 1) Parameters data int[] Array of position data to set in GenData tableNum int ECAM table number (1-10, default: 1) Remarks The data array will be written to the GenData array starting from the configured start index. Make sure the data array size matches the configured table range. ECAM_SetTableRange(int, int, int) Set ECAM table range (start and end indices in GenData array). void ECAM_SetTableRange(int startIndex, int endIndex, int tableNum = 1) Parameters startIndex int Start index in GenData array endIndex int End index in GenData array tableNum int ECAM table number (1-10, default: 1) Remarks This sets the range in the GenData array where the ECAM table data is stored. ECAM_Start(int) Start ECAM motion with specified table. bool ECAM_Start(int tableNum = 1) Parameters tableNum int ECAM table number to use (1-10, default: 1) Returns bool Returns true if ECAM motion started successfully, otherwise false. Remarks Before starting ECAM motion, ensure that: ECAM table is properly configured with ECAM_ConfigureTable ECAM table data is set with ECAM_SetTableData Master axis is properly configured ECAM_Stop() Stop ECAM motion. bool ECAM_Stop() Returns bool Returns true if ECAM motion stopped successfully, otherwise false. Remarks This will immediately stop the current ECAM motion and return the axis to normal operation.

Interface IGroupAxis Namespace AAMotion Assembly AAMotion.dll IGroupAxis interface definition, used to describe the parameters and states related to the CNC group axes public interface IGroupAxis Properties CNCAEmrgDec CNC vector deceleration used during emergency stop (e.g., when hardware positive/negative limit switches are triggered, or software positive/negative limit positions are reached). CNCAPosRef, CNCAdPosRef int CNCAEmrgDec { get; set; } Property Value int CNCAEncRatio This parameter is axis-related and should be set individually for each member axis. It defines the ratio between the resolution of one axis and other axes, used for more accurate CNC motion calculation when member axes have inconsistent physical resolutions. Currently, this parameter is reserved for future use. int CNCAEncRatio { get; set; } Property Value int CNCAPercents Scale factor for user adjustment of speed (and acceleration/deceleration) along the CNC path. By affecting speed and acceleration/deceleration, CNCAPercents actually influences the time required to complete CNC motion. CNCAPercents can be greater than 100% and can be dynamically adjusted at any time. Users should consider the value of CNCAPercents before starting CNC motion. int CNCAPercents { get; set; } Property Value int CNCAPosRef CNCAPosRef represents the expected position along the CNC path (starting from zero, reaching CNCAAbsTrgt at the end of the motion segment). int CNCAPosRef { get; } Property Value int CNCAStatus Containing CNC-related status data. The meaning of each index is as follows: Index 1: Oldest command Index 2: Last pushed command Index 3: Last segment command Index 4: Total number of parameters in the last segment Index 5: Last segment requires multiple parameters to be pushed Index 6: Motion segment input Index 7: Available space Index 8: Last used ID Index 9: ID in motion Index 10: CNC FIFO motion status
  • BIT_0: CNC in motion
  • BIT_3: CNC stop request issued
  • BIT_4: CNC accelerating
  • BIT_5: CNC decelerating
  • BIT_6: CNC waiting for end smoothing
  • BIT_9: CNC waiting for input
  • BIT_12: CNC in CNC stop state
  • BIT_13: CNC waiting for first segment
  • BIT_14: CNC controlled stop request issued
Index 11: CNC FIFO member axes Index 12: CNC FIFO involved axes Index 13: Maximum acceleration counter Index 14: Maximum velocity fluctuation counter When the status is invalid, its value is -1 (when the status is valid, -1 is not a valid value for any status). api/AAMotion.IIOModule.html.summary: Interface IIOModule Namespace AAMotion Assembly AAMotion.dll IIOModule interface definition, used to describe the parameters and states related to the IO module public interface IIOModule Properties AInDB Analog input deadband (unit: mV). If the input voltage is between (-AInDB) and AInDB, the reading is 0; If it exceeds AInDB, the reading is (actual voltage - AInDB); If it is below (-AInDB), the reading is (actual voltage + AInDB). - Old firmware (int type): Integer deadband values in millivolts. - New firmware (float type): Float deadband values in millivolts. Returns dynamic type to support both int (old firmware) and float (new firmware). AInOffSet , AInGain , AInFilt , AInPort dynamic AInDB { get; } Property Value dynamic AInFilt Analog input filter coefficient array. AInFilt[i] determines the filter coefficient for the i-th analog input. - Old firmware (int type): Integer coefficients (65536 = no filtering, i.e., C1=1). - New firmware (float type): Direct float coefficient values. Returns dynamic type to support both int (old firmware) and float (new firmware). AInOffSet , AInDB , AInGain , AInPort dynamic AInFilt { get; } Property Value dynamic AInGain Analog input gain array. - Old firmware (int type): Actual gain = AInGain / 65536. When gain is 1, AInGain=65536. - New firmware (float type): Direct float value. When gain is 1, AInGain=1.0. Returns dynamic type to support both int (old firmware) and float (new firmware). AInOffSet , AInDB , AInFilt , AInPort dynamic AInGain { get; } Property Value dynamic AInMode Analog input mode configuration array. Each element defines the function of the corresponding analog input point. Common function values: 0 - General input 1 - Velocity command 2 - Current command 3 - Force feedback 4 - Force command 5 - Joystick input 6 - Torque compensation 7 - Negative torque limit 8 - Positive torque limit 9 - Speed feedback Others - Unknown AAValueArray<int> AInMode { get; } Property Value AAValueArray<int> AInOffSet Analog input offset (unit: mV). The value of AInOffset[i] will be added to the actual input voltage. - Old firmware (int type): Integer offset values in millivolts. - New firmware (float type): Float offset values in millivolts. Returns dynamic type to support both int (old firmware) and float (new firmware). AInDB , AInGain , AInFilt , AInPort dynamic AInOffSet { get; } Property Value dynamic AInPort Read-only array containing processed and raw values of analog input ports. The first half: processed values (filtered, offset, deadband, gain applied) for each channel; The second half: raw input values for each channel (unprocessed). - Old firmware (int type): Integer values representing raw ADC counts. - New firmware (float type): Float values representing actual voltage/processed values. Returns dynamic type to support both int (old firmware) and float (new firmware). AInFilt, AInDB, AInGain, AInOffSet dynamic AInPort { get; } Property Value dynamic AOutMode AOutMode determines the parameter monitored by each analog output channel. AOutMode[i] specifies the parameter reflected by the i-th analog output. The structure of AOutMode (32-bit integer): - Bits 0~9 (LSB, 10 bits): CAN code of the parameter - Bits 10~12 (3 bits): Axis number (0 is the first axis) - Bits 16~31 (16 bits): Array index (ignored if not used) AOutPort , AOutOffset , AOutShifts AAValueArray<int> AOutMode { get; } Property Value AAValueArray<int> AOutOffset Analog output offset (unit: mV). The value of AOutOffset[i] will be added to the actual output voltage for calibration or adjustment. AAValueArray<int> AOutOffset { get; } Property Value AAValueArray<int> AOutPort Direct analog output (unit: mV). When AOutMode[i]=0, the value of AOutPort[i] is directly output to the i-th analog output. AOutMode , AOutShifts AAValueArray<int> AOutPort { get; } Property Value AAValueArray<int> AOutShifts Analog output shift factor. AOutShifts[i] is used to adjust the dynamic range of the i-th analog output (in conjunction with the parameter monitored by AOutMode). If AOutShifts is negative, right shift (divide by 2 to the power of |AOutShifts|); if positive, left shift (multiply by 2 to the power of AOutShifts). AOutMode , AOutPort AAValueArray<int> AOutShifts { get; } Property Value AAValueArray<int> BiDirConfig Input bidirectional differential direction configuration. Selects between input and output mode for each input independently. 0 - input, 1 - output. int BiDirConfig { get; set; } Property Value int DInFilt Pulse/direction input filter, in sampling cycles (80MHz). The input value is updated only if the result is consistent for DInFilt consecutive samples. int DInFilt { get; set; } Property Value int DInLog Digital input logic inversion control. Each bit corresponds to an input point: 0 - normal logic (On returns 1, Off returns 0), 1 - inverted logic (On returns 0, Off returns 1). DInPort,DInFilt,DInMode int DInLog { get; set; } Property Value int DInLogHigh int DInLogHigh { get; set; } Property Value int DInMode Discrete input mode configuration array. Each element defines the function of the corresponding input point. Common function values (see documentation): 0 - General input 2 - Servo enable 3 - Start motion 4 - Stop motion 5 - Clear input pulse 7 - Clear fault/alarm 8 - Abort motion 9 - RLS (reverse limit) 10 - FLS (forward limit) 11 - Torque limit on 12 - Activate dynamic break 13 - Activate motor brake 14 - Change control filter set 15 - Add velocity filter 16 - Velocity/Position mode switch 17 - Velocity/Current mode switch 18 - Position/Current mode switch 19 - Clear absolute encoder 20 - Change speed 21 - Home 22 - Mode switch between Position Operation Mode and Force Operation Mode 23 - Hall A 24 - Fault input 25 - HomingOn input DOutMode, DInPort, DInLog, DOutPort AAValueArray<int> DInMode { get; } Property Value AAValueArray<int> DInPort Gets the status of the digital input port. The return value is a decimal integer, each bit represents the status of a digital input point. DInLog,DInFilt,DInMode,DInPortHigh int DInPort { get; } Property Value int DInPortHigh Gets the status of the high digital input port. The return value is a decimal integer, each bit represents the status of a high input point. int DInPortHigh { get; } Property Value int DOutLog Digital output logic inversion control. Each bit corresponds to an output point: 0 - normal logic (DOutPort=1 outputs "On", 0 outputs "Off"), 1 - inverted logic (1 outputs "Off", 0 outputs "On"). Note: The 0th bit (LSB) of DOutLog corresponds to output 1. DOutMode, DOutMode, DOutPort int DOutLog { get; set; } Property Value int DOutMode Digital output mode configuration array. Each element defines the special function of the corresponding output point. Value and function: 0 - Normal output (controlled by DOutPort) 1 - Dedicated hardware function (not used) 2 - Servo enable (reflects MotorOn status) 3 - In motion (reflects MotionStat status) 4 - Accelerating (reflects MotionStat acceleration bit, only valid in built-in analyzer mode) 5 - Decelerating (reflects MotionStat deceleration bit, only valid in built-in analyzer mode) 6 - Constant speed (reflects MotionStat constant speed bit, only valid in built-in analyzer mode) 7 - Motion end (not used) 8 - Target reached (reflects InTargetStat=4) 9 - Fault/alarm (reflects ConFlt status) 10 - Last motion warning (not used) 11 - Last motion saturation (not used) 12 - RLS/FLS active (reflects LimitsStat status) 13 - Out of travel (RevPLim, FwdPLim) 14 - Regeneration active 15 - Dynamic brake active 16 - Motor brake active (can be used with DInMode[i]=13) If multiple outputs are assigned the same special function, the output with the higher number has priority. DInMode, DOutPort, DOutLog, DInPort AAValueArray<int> DOutMode { get; } Property Value AAValueArray<int> DOutPort Discrete output port status. Each bit corresponds to an output point (0th bit is output 1). Actual output is affected by DOutLog (XOR inversion), DOutMode (special function), and DOutSelect (signal source selection). DOutMode, DOutLog, DOutType, DOutSelect int DOutPort { get; set; } Property Value int DOutSelect Digital output function selection array. 0: Software DOutPort (normal output controlled by DOutPort, DOutLog, DOutMode, DOutPortSB, DOutPortCB) 1: Reserved or predefined function (differential output, see below) Differential output 1 (DOutPort bit 4): Axis A encoder emulation A Differential output 2 (DOutPort bit 5): Axis A encoder emulation B Differential output 3 (DOutPort bit 6): Axis A encoder emulation Z Differential output 4 (DOutPort bit 7): Axis A encoder emulation pulse 2: A event #1 3: A event #2 4: A event #3 5: B event #1 6: B event #2 7: B event #3 8: C event #1 9: C event #2 10: C event #3 11: UserPWM 1 12: UserPWM 2 DOutPort , DOutMode ,EventType ,UserPWM . AAValueArray<int> DOutSelect { get; } Property Value AAValueArray<int> DOutType Digital output type configuration. Each bit corresponds to an output point: 0 - open collector (pull-down, default), 1 - open collector (pull-up). Note: The 0th bit (LSB) corresponds to output 1. DOutMode, DOutLog, DOutPort int DOutType { get; set; } Property Value int Methods DOutClearBit(int) Clear the specified digital output bit DOutPort bool DOutClearBit(int index) Parameters index int Index of the digital output bit to clear Returns bool Returns true if the command is sent successfully, otherwise false DOutSetBit(int) Set the specified digital output bit DOutPort bool DOutSetBit(int index) Parameters index int Index of the digital output bit to set Returns bool Returns true if the command is sent successfully, otherwise false DOutToggleBit(int) Toggle the specified digital output bit DOutPort bool DOutToggleBit(int index) Parameters index int Index of the digital output bit to toggle Returns bool Returns true if the command is sent successfully, otherwise false GetDInPort(int) Gets the current state of a specific digital input bit int GetDInPort(int bit) Parameters bit int 0-based bit index (0-31) Returns int State of the specified bit (0 = Off, 1 = On).It is also necessary to refer to DOutLog GetDOutPort(int) Gets the current state of a specific digital output bit int GetDOutPort(int bit) Parameters bit int 0-based bit index (0-31) Returns int State of the specified bit (0 = Off, 1 = On).It is also necessary to refer to DInLog

articles/getting-started/aamotion.html.title: AAMotion - Getting Started | Agito AAMotion SDK
articles/getting-started/aamotion.html.summary: AAMotion AAMotion is a C# .NET API for advanced motion controller communication and control, designed for high-performance and flexible integration with industrial motion systems. 📚 API documentation: https://akribis-agito.github.io/Agito-Releases/aamotion/ 🌐 Vendor: https://agito-akribis.com Overview AAMotion provides a comprehensive interface for connecting to, configuring, and controlling a wide range of motion controllers. The API supports both high-level and low-level operations, enabling users to perform tasks such as initialization, connection, axis control, IO operations, and advanced motion programming. Supported platforms: Windows 7 or later Supported frameworks: .NET Framework 4.8 Documentation: API documentation is available via IntelliSense (XML doc comments included with the package). System Requirements Microsoft Windows 7 or later .NET Framework 4.8 Visual Studio 2010 or later (other IDEs may be used, but are not officially supported) Installation Install the NuGet package from nuget.org: .dotnet add package Agito.AAMotion Or via the NuGet Package Manager in Visual Studio. Note: The package may require additional dependencies such as YamlDotNet. These are automatically handled by NuGet. Getting Started Create a new C# project targeting .NET Framework 4.8. Add the Agito.AAMotion NuGet package. Explore the API via IntelliSense — XML doc comments are included with the package. Usage Example Below is a minimal example demonstrating how to initialize a controller, connect to it, perform basic axis operations, and shut down: using System; using System.Diagnostics; using AAMotion; namespace ConsoleApp1 { class Program { static void Main(string[] args) { const string ip = "172.1.1.101"; // the controller's factory default MotionController controller = AAMotionAPI.Initialize(ControllerType.AGM800); try { Console.WriteLine($"Connecting to {ip}"); controller.Init(); Stopwatch stopwatch = new Stopwatch(); stopwatch.Start(); bool isConnected = AAMotionAPI.Connect(controller, ip); stopwatch.Stop(); Console.WriteLine($"Connect execution time: {stopwatch.ElapsedMilliseconds} ms"); if (isConnected) { Console.WriteLine("Connect successful"); AAMotionAPI.MotorOn(controller, AxisRef.B); // Example: perform additional axis or IO operations here } else { Console.WriteLine("Connect failed"); } } finally { AAMotionAPI.MotorOff(controller, AxisRef.B); Console.WriteLine($"MotorOff status for Axis A: {controller.GetAxis(AxisRef.A).MotorOn}"); // Release THIS controller's resources. The shared AACommServer keeps running // for other clients; controller.Shutdown() would request a server shutdown, // which the server honors only when this is its last client — call it only // when you own the machine's comms lifecycle. controller.Dispose(); } } } } API Documentation API documentation is available via IntelliSense. XML doc comments are included with the NuGet package. Release Notes See CHANGELOG.md for detailed release notes and version history. License This software is proprietary. All rights reserved. Contact Agito for licensing and usage terms. For further information, consult the included documentation or contact Agito support.

articles/getting-started/native-c-sdk.ht.title: Native C SDK (aamotion.h) | Agito AAMotion SDK
articles/getting-started/native-c-sdk.ht.summary: AAMotion Native SDK A native C ABI over the high-level AAMotion client — drive an Agito motion controller from C, C++, Python, or any language with a C FFI, with no .NET runtime on the target. The library is NativeAOT-compiled per platform and ships as a single shared library plus two headers. It replaces the retired Windows-only C++/CLI AAMotionCPP + AGAAMotion. Platform Library Link with Windows x64 aamotion.dll aamotion.lib (import lib) Linux x64 libaamotion.so -laamotion macOS x64 / arm64 libaamotion.dylib -laamotion Every platform ships the same two headers: aamotion.h (the API) and aamotion_enums.h (aamotion_controller_type_t / aamotion_axis_ref_t and the status/descriptor enums, generated from the AAMotion C# enums — the single source of truth). aamotion.h is the authoritative per-function reference; this guide is the conceptual overview. Status: validated on win-x64 against a live AGM800 (connect, reads, motor on/off, relative / absolute / jog motion, GenData read/write, IO, and the enum/error description getters all exercised under NativeAOT). linux-x64 builds and packs in CI; macOS builds are pending a build runner. Getting the library .NET (P/Invoke): add the Agito.AAMotion.Native NuGet — aamotion.dll / libaamotion.so lands next to your build output automatically; [DllImport("aamotion")]. C / C++: take the C/C++ archive (the include/ headers + per-RID native libs, the AACommServerNative AACS daemon, and a sample). The session opens a server implicitly on first connect, so keep the daemon beside the library; no .NET runtime is required on the target. Python / other FFI: drop the platform library beside your script and ctypes.CDLL it (it is inside both artifacts above). A ctypes-over-native AAMotionPy wheel is a possible future consumer of this channel — not built yet. From source: build each RID on its own OS (NativeAOT cannot cross-compile) with dotnet publish -r <rid>. Distribution note: the Agito.AAMotion.Native NuGet and the C/C++ archive (win-x64 + linux-x64) ship on the public Software/AAMotion-Native release line at https://github.com/akribis-agito/Agito-Releases/releases, alongside each managed Agito.AAMotion release. They are not on nuget.org — the C ABI is exact-match gated pre-1.0 and the package carries only the RIDs above. The package version is locked to the managed Agito.AAMotion. Architecture in one paragraph The SDK is a client, exactly like the AAComm native SDK. It wraps the managed net8 AAMotion client, which in turn talks to AACS (the AAComm server) — a separate, shared process that owns the actual controller connection. aamotion_initialize brings up / attaches to a local AACS automatically (the managed connect path spawns or locates it), then aamotion_connect opens a controller channel through it. AACS is not embedded in the SDK; it is resolved/launched as its own process. AAMotion is the motion layer (motor on/off, point-to-point and interpolated moves, homing, IO, force, vector, PEG, CNC groups, program control); for raw controller-message traffic the AAComm native SDK is the lower layer. Quick start — C / C++ #include "aamotion.h" #include <stdio.h> int main(void) { /* aamotion_initialize brings up / attaches to AACS and builds a controller of the given type. AAMOTION_CONTROLLER_TYPE_AGM800 == 10 (the ProductTypes ID, from aamotion_enums.h). */ aamotion_controller c = aamotion_initialize(AAMOTION_CONTROLLER_TYPE_AGM800); if (!c) return 1; /* aamotion_connect to the controller through AACS. fastArk / enableAutoReconnect are 0/1 flags. */ if (aamotion_connect(c, "172.1.1.101", 0, 0)) /* factory-default address */ { aamotion_motor_on(c, AAMOTION_AXIS_REF_A); /* AAMOTION_AXIS_REF_A == 1 */ aamotion_move_relative(c, AAMOTION_AXIS_REF_A, 10000, 5000, 100000, 100000); /* dist, speed, accel, decel */ char reply[256]; if (aamotion_send_command_string(c, "APos", reply, (int)sizeof(reply))) printf("APos -> %s\n", reply); aamotion_motor_off(c, AAMOTION_AXIS_REF_A); } aamotion_disconnect(c); /* closes the link AND frees the handle */ aamotion_release(c); /* safe even after aamotion_disconnect — Free is null/double-free tolerant */ return 0; } Build (Windows, from a x64 Native Tools prompt or after vcvars64): cl /nologo sample.c /I path\to\include /link path\to\aamotion.lib :: aamotion.dll must sit next to the .exe or on PATH at run time Build (Linux / macOS): cc sample.c -I path/to/include -L path/to/lib -laamotion -o sample LD_LIBRARY_PATH=path/to/lib ./sample # macOS: DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH Quick start — Python (ctypes) No bindings package required — load the shared library directly. Set restype / argtypes so the opaque handle and the bool/buffer arguments marshal correctly. At the ABI a C bool is a 1-byte 0/1, so declare it ctypes.c_bool. import ctypes lib = ctypes.CDLL("./libaamotion.so") # "aamotion.dll" on Windows, "libaamotion.dylib" on macOS # Opaque handle is void*. aamotion_initialize takes a aamotion_controller_type_t int and returns the handle. lib.aamotion_initialize.restype = ctypes.c_void_p lib.aamotion_initialize.argtypes = [ctypes.c_int] lib.aamotion_connect.restype = ctypes.c_bool lib.aamotion_connect.argtypes = [ctypes.c_void_p, ctypes.c_char_p, ctypes.c_bool, ctypes.c_bool] lib.aamotion_motor_on.argtypes = [ctypes.c_void_p, ctypes.c_int] lib.aamotion_motor_on.restype = ctypes.c_bool lib.aamotion_move_relative.argtypes = [ctypes.c_void_p, ctypes.c_int, ctypes.c_int, ctypes.c_int, ctypes.c_int, ctypes.c_int] lib.aamotion_move_relative.restype = ctypes.c_bool lib.aamotion_send_command_string.argtypes = [ctypes.c_void_p, ctypes.c_char_p, ctypes.c_char_p, ctypes.c_int] lib.aamotion_send_command_string.restype = ctypes.c_bool AGM800 = 10 # AAMOTION_CONTROLLER_TYPE_AGM800 AXIS_A = 1 # AAMOTION_AXIS_REF_A c = lib.aamotion_initialize(AGM800) if c and lib.aamotion_connect(c, b"172.1.1.101", False, False): # factory-default address lib.aamotion_motor_on(c, AXIS_A) lib.aamotion_move_relative(c, AXIS_A, 10000, 5000, 100000, 100000) # dist, speed, accel, decel buf = ctypes.create_string_buffer(256) if lib.aamotion_send_command_string(c, b"APos", buf, 256): print("APos ->", buf.value.decode()) lib.aamotion_motor_off(c, AXIS_A) lib.aamotion_disconnect(c) # closes the link AND frees the handle lib.aamotion_release(c) # safe after aamotion_disconnect To receive controller error events, declare the matching CFUNCTYPE and register it. Keep a Python reference to the CFUNCTYPE instance for as long as it can fire — if it is garbage-collected the library calls a freed trampoline: ERROR_CB = ctypes.CFUNCTYPE(None, ctypes.c_int, ctypes.c_char_p, ctypes.c_char_p) def _on_error(code, message, exception): print("error", code, message.decode() if message else "", exception.decode() if exception else "") error_cb = ERROR_CB(_on_error) # keep this alive for the session lib.aamotion_set_error_occurred_handler.argtypes = [ctypes.c_void_p, ERROR_CB] lib.aamotion_set_error_occurred_handler(c, error_cb) Core contracts Handle lifecycle aamotion_initialize(controllerType) returns an opaque aamotion_controller handle (a token from an internal handle table mapping to a managed AAMotion aamotion_controller — never a raw pointer, so a stale or forged handle resolves to nothing instead of undefined behavior), or NULL on failure — including an unknown controller type and an AACS that could not be spawned/reached. One handle owns at most one controller connection. Free it with aamotion_release(h) — or aamotion_disconnect(h), which closes the link and frees the handle. The teardown is null- and double-free-tolerant: the C++/CLI predecessor's contract of calling both aamotion_disconnect (which frees) and a later aamotion_release is safe, and a NULL/stale handle degrades gracefully (every export returns false/0 rather than crashing). For concurrent controllers, create multiple handles. The optical-coupling API adds a second opaque handle, aamotion_optical_coupling, built from a controller handle with aamotion_optical_coupling_create(h) and freed with aamotion_optical_coupling_release(oc). It does not own the controller connection — release it before releasing the controller handle it was created from. The connect sequence aamotion_initialize(controllerType) — builds the controller and brings up / attaches to AACS. Pass a aamotion_controller_type_t value from aamotion_enums.h (e.g. AAMOTION_CONTROLLER_TYPE_AGM800 = 10) — these are the product-type IDs, not ordinals. aamotion_connect(h, deviceAddress, fastArk, enableAutoReconnect) — opens the controller channel through AACS (e.g. the factory-default Ethernet IP "172.1.1.101"). fastArk / enableAutoReconnect are bool. Returns true on success. aamotion_is_connected(h) — true while the channel is open and (for IP-connected controllers) the device answers an ICMP ping the call performs synchronously; with auto-reconnect enabled a failed probe runs a full reconnect attempt inline (seconds to tens of seconds worst case, 5 s cooldown). Not a cheap flag read — budget polling accordingly. aamotion_disconnect(h) — closes the channel and frees the handle; or aamotion_release(h) to free without a prior disconnect. bool and result conventions Most exports return a C bool — true on success, false on failure (a 1-byte 0/1 at the ABI). A NULL handle, a NULL string argument, an unresolvable/stale handle, or an internal exception all map to false/0 — exceptions never cross the boundary. This bool-return convention is deliberately different from aacomm.*'s uniform aacomm_status return: aamotion.* keeps the success/failure contract of the retired AGAAMotion wrapper it replaces, so the two SDKs are each internally consistent rather than mutually identical. int-returning getters (aamotion_read_gen_data, aamotion_get_d_out_port, aamotion_get_d_in_port, and the whole Slow-Logger and optical-coupling read families) return the controller value directly — and return 0 on any failure (bad handle, not connected, controller ERR), indistinguishable from a legitimate 0. When that matters, read via aamotion_send_command_string and check its bool instead. void fire-and-forget setters (the aamotion_force_curr_set_* family, the PEG/lock setters, aamotion_set_vector_param, the two-speed aamotion_move_*_two_speed non-wait variants, …) give no success feedback at all — mirroring AGAAMotion's void contract. Failures still surface through the error callback; use it (or a follow-up read) when you need confirmation of a setter. Per-axis int axis arguments take an aamotion_axis_ref_t bit value (AAMOTION_AXIS_REF_A = 1, AAMOTION_AXIS_REF_B = 2, … combinable). A plain int speed/accel/decel is passed verbatim — 0 is a literal 0, not "use default". Strings: the fixed-buffer contract Output strings are UTF-8. The string functions — aamotion_send_command_string / aamotion_send_bulk_command_string, the Get*Des enum-description getters, and aamotion_get_error_description_by_code — take a caller-supplied writable buffer plus its size (char* buf, int size): the result is written truncated to fit and always NUL-terminated. The Get* description getters return true when a non-empty description was written, false (writing nothing) on an unknown value, empty result, or NULL/zero buffer. aamotion_send_bulk_command_string is Ethernet-only. The error callback Register a session-level error handler with: typedef void (*aamotion_error_occurred_cb)(int errorCode, const char* message, const char* exception); void aamotion_set_error_occurred_handler(aamotion_controller h, aamotion_error_occurred_cb cb); void aamotion_clear_error_occurred_handler(aamotion_controller h); The callback fires on AAMotion's firing thread, never on your calling thread — keep it short and thread-safe; marshal real work to your own thread/queue. The const char* arguments (message, exception) are owned by the library and valid only for the duration of the call — copy them if you need them later; do not free them. Only one handler is held per handle; a later aamotion_set_error_occurred_handler replaces the earlier one, and aamotion_clear_error_occurred_handler removes it. Enum and error descriptions The Get*Des(int value, char* buf, int size) family maps an integer value of the matching enum in aamotion_enums.h to its human-readable description (e.g. aamotion_get_con_flt_des(1003, …) → "Encoder disconnected"). aamotion_get_error_description_by_code(int errorCode, …) resolves a controller error code. Both follow the fixed-buffer contract above. API reference aamotion.h is the authoritative per-function reference. aamotion.h itself. The status/descriptor enums carry a _t suffix so they don't collide with the like-named ABI functions (e.g. the aamotion_motor_on() export vs the aamotion_motor_on_t enum). Always build against the headers that ship with your library. ABI versioning & stability int32_t aamotion_abi_version(void); The SDK carries two version numbers, for two different purposes: Package version — the SemVer of the aamotion.* library / Agito.AAMotion.Native NuGet, version-locked to the managed Agito.AAMotion ($(AAMotionVersion); the native package ships on its own release line off the back of each managed release — see AAComm/docs/native-aot-sdk.md). This is what you pin in a package reference. aamotion_abi_version() — a soname-style breaking-generation number, the C-ABI contract. It is bumped only on a breaking change: a changed or removed export signature, a callback-signature change, or changed semantics. Additive changes — new exports, new enum values — never bump it (they cannot break a compiled consumer). It returns its value directly (it cannot fail) and takes no handle; the same value is the AAMOTION_ABI_VERSION macro in the generated aamotion_enums.h. Generation 1 is the first shipped ABI (pre-release increments carried no compatibility meaning and were reset). Consumer rule — exact-match gate. Call aamotion_abi_version() once at load and reject a library whose value does not equal AAMOTION_ABI_VERSION from the headers your binding was built against — coherent with the bump policy, because the number only moves when your binary genuinely cannot run. The committed include/aamotion.abi.txt records the exact export surface for the generation; aamotion_enums.h and the manifest are generated from the C# source and CI diff-gated, while aamotion.h is hand-maintained — the manifest diff is what forces it to be updated in review. Always build against the aamotion.h that ships with the library you load. Release notes CHANGELOG.md — package version tracks Agito.AAMotion in lockstep; the C-ABI contract is the separate aamotion_abi_version() integer described above. See also In the repo (AACommComponents/): AAMotionNative/include/aamotion.h — the authoritative C ABI (per-function; also in the sdk zip). AAMotionNative/include/aamotion_enums.h — generated aamotion_controller_type_t / aamotion_axis_ref_t / status enums. AAComm/docs/native-aot-sdk.md — the native-channel design, architecture, and status (§Motion layer). AACommNative/README.md — the lower-level AAComm native SDK (raw controller messaging). docs/changelog-template.md — the changelog shape every shipped component keeps.

articles/release-notes/aamotion-changelo.title: AAMotion Changelog | Agito AAMotion SDK
articles/release-notes/aamotion-changelo.summary: Changelog All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file. The format is based on Keep a Changelog, and this project adheres to Semantic Versioning. [11.0.0] - 2026-08-26 ⚠️ Breaking AAMotion.dll is now strong-named (PublicKeyToken=043a10799a9b732b, the same key as Agito.AAComm 14.x), so strong-named consumers can reference it. .NET Framework consumers must recompile against 11.0.0 — a binary built against a 10.x AAMotion, PublicKeyToken=null reference does not bind to the signed assembly (see the Agito.AAComm 14.0.0 changelog for the details; the same identity change and AssemblyVersion pinning, here 11.0.0.0, apply). .NET 8/10 consumers see no difference. Requires Agito.AAComm 14.x (see its changelog for the breaking communication-layer changes — long-operation events, binary IPC v3, protocol negotiation). AAMotionAPI.WriteUserParam(controller, AxisRef, index, value) is renamed GroupWriteUserParam — it issues the CNC group-buffered write (command 9), not a direct register write, and the old name collided with the new direct WriteUserParam(controller, index, value) (see Added). The IGroupAxis.WriteUserParam member keeps its name (the receiver disambiguates); the Java binding follows the facade rename. AAMotionAPI.OpendAACommServer() is renamed OpenAACommServer() (typo fix). AAMotionAPI.ForceCurr_SetSlowApproache is renamed ForceCurr_SetSlowApproach (typo fix) — also on ISingleAxis, the native ABI export, and the Java binding. MotionController.ErrorOccurred and CommAPIInterface.ErrorOccurred are now event members (were public delegate fields). +=/-= subscriptions recompile as-is; direct assignment or external invocation no longer compiles. Fixed Connect no longer returns false on a busy machine while the server is running. It gates on CommAPI.IsAACommServerRunning, whose loopback probe used to depend on ThreadPool scheduling and so reported a listening server as absent under CPU pressure — reported only through a Debug.WriteLine, making it look like a silent connect failure. Fixed in AAComm; see its changelog. AAMotionAPI.AutoCorner: the cornerAxes argument was incorrectly passed to GetGroup(), whose dictionary keys are only AxisRef.A (or AxisRef.B on AGM800). Every call path was broken — GetGroup(axis) with axis = AxisRef.A resolved to a 1-axis group (rejected by the controller as CNC_FIFO_WRONG_NUM_OF_INVOLVED_AXES), and axis = AxisRef.A | AxisRef.B caused a KeyNotFoundException on the unguarded indexer. Now resolves the group via GetGroup(AxisRef.A) like all other CNC facade methods, and forwards the full mask to the wire segment. Source- and binary-compatible; no signature or ABI change. Added Native aamotion.* C-ABI SDK (Agito.AAMotion.Native): a NativeAOT shared library (aamotion.dll / libaamotion.so / libaamotion.dylib + aamotion.h) exposing the full flat motion surface (199 functions, each aamotion_ + the managed name in snake_case, constants AAMOTION_*) over the AAMotion client with no .NET runtime on the target, for C / C++ / Python (ctypes) consumers. Packaged as the Agito.AAMotion.Native NuGet (runtimes/<rid>/native/, for .NET P/Invoke) and an agito-aamotion-native-sdk-*.zip C/C++ archive, version-locked to Agito.AAMotion and published together on the public Software/AAMotion-Native release line at https://github.com/akribis-agito/Agito-Releases/releases — not on nuget.org, because the C ABI is exact-match gated pre-1.0. win-x64 (HW-proven on AGM800) and linux-x64 ship; osx pends its build runner. AAMotionAPI.UploadParameters() / DownloadParameters(): New static methods on AAMotionAPI that upload controller parameters to a .par file or download parameters from a .par file to the controller. Follows the PCSuite "Parameters Upload/Download" convention: upload queries all supported parameters and writes them with a header (product type, firmware/FPGA version, date, checksum) to an ASCII .par file; download reads the .par file, validates parameter compatibility, then writes each as a SET command. Ethernet connections use Bulk messages (up to 50 per packet); other channels send one by one. After a successful download, optionally sends ASave plus per-axis CalcFilters to persist parameters to flash. ISingleAxis.MoveAbsRepetitiveCycle() / AAMotionAPI.MoveAbsRepetitiveCycle(): New method on ISingleAxis / SingleAxis and a corresponding static wrapper on AAMotionAPI that moves the axis to an absolute position repeatedly for a finite number of cycles with a dwell time at each end point. rptCycles = 0 requests infinite cycles (controller default). The method sets RptMode = 0, RptCycles = {rptCycles}, RelTrgt = 0, AbsTrgt = {position}, RptWait = {msDwellTime}, MotionMode = 2, then issues Begin. The package now also ships a net10.0 target (alongside net48 and net8.0) — matching Agito.AAComm 14.x; .NET 10 is the current LTS runtime. Two-speed point-to-point moves: ISingleAxis/AAMotionAPI MoveAbsTwoSpeed(AndWait) / MoveRelTwoSpeed(AndWait) — the move runs at speed1 and switches to speed2 when crossing speedChangePosition (Abs) / after speedChangeDistance (Rel), for slow-approach flows (bonding, dispensing). The optional speedChgDir (0 = forward, 1 = reverse crossing) defaults to 0 on Abs and to the distance sign on Rel; the native ABI takes it as a plain int where a negative value selects that default. Direct GenData/UserParam register I/O in float and double widths: MotionController/AAMotionAPI ReadGenDataF/ReadGenDataD, WriteGenDataF/WriteGenDataD, ReadUserParam/ReadUserParamF/ReadUserParamD, WriteUserParam/WriteUserParamF/WriteUserParamD (writes A<reg>[i]=v directly, complementing the int-typed ReadGenData/WriteGenData), backed by the new eKeyword.UserParam/UserParamF/UserParamD mappings. Optical coupling light-finding API: new OpticalCouplingLightFinding class in AAMotion/Shared/OpticalCouplingLightFinding.cs providing a 2-step workflow (parameter configuration, then start) for optical alignment processes. Supports spiral scan (ScanType.Spiral = 1) and single-axis scan (ScanType.SingleAxis = 5). Exposes configuration properties mapped to controller AGenData registers (e.g. ScanCode, CouplingAxis, SpiralPitch, MaxScanSpeed, OptimalCoeff). Provides typed result models: SpiralScanResult and SingleAxisScanResult with coupling result, error code, sampled positions, and channel power data. Includes helper methods to start scans, apply configurations, read sampled arrays, and batch-sync AGenData via SyncAllGenData. Fixed AAMotionAPI.OpenAACommServer(string) and CommAPIInterface.OpenAACommServer(string) now spawn the server through the AAComm spawn contract (headless + redirected stdin, correct working directory, socket-ready polling with a child-death probe) instead of a bare Process.Start + fixed 1.5 s sleep — a slow cold start, a lost bind race, or an interactive native host no longer yields a false "started" (or a TUI taking over the consumer's terminal). AAMotionAPI.OpenAACommServer() no longer latches "started" after a FAILED start: the first failure (missing sidecar, blocked port) previously made every later call a silent no-op even after the environment was fixed. The *AndWait motion waits (MoveAbsAndWait, MoveRelAndWait, the two-speed and repetitive variants) now poll the controller's in-target status live, never through the FastReadCache. With FastReadEnabled, a cached pre-move InTargetStat=4 (the axis parked on its previous target) — or a value stranded by a link failure, which never invalidates cache entries — could satisfy the wait instantly, reporting "target reached" for a move that never happened. MotionController.TryReconnect no longer trusts the raw socket alone: a logically-connected link is verified by ping (where the address is a real IP) before the call short-circuits to success, so a pulled cable / network partition now triggers a real disconnect-and-reconnect instead of "reconnected" with a dead link — this also makes IsConnected's auto-reconnect path honest. With no requested address and no last known address the call now fails instead of silently targeting a hardcoded default IP (a reachable but unintended controller could be connected). A successful reconnect to an explicit new address now updates the last known address, so reachability probes and later reconnects track the live link, not the device the controller left behind. SendBulkCommandString no longer reports success when an error rides in a non-first segment of the bulk reply (e.g. OK>OK>ERR 4010) — the whole-reply error flag misses embedded segments, so classification is now per-segment against the full reply taxonomy (ERR / BOOT ERR / PC Suite: ERR). Controller replies carrying int/long values are now parsed culture-invariantly, matching the float/double path. On a machine whose culture uses a non-ASCII negative sign (several ICU cultures on modern .NET), a negative reply like -123 failed to parse and read as 0; parameter values written to the controller now also format invariantly on every path. MotionController.IsConnected no longer reports false for healthy non-IP connections: the ICMP reachability probe now runs only when the controller was connected via a real IP address — a Simulator / serial / CAN connection reports the logical connection state (previously the unparseable address failed the ping and the property was permanently false), and when no address is known the property no longer pings a hardcoded default IP (another device's reachability was reported as this controller's). Bulk parameter upload/download keeps request↔reply alignment: an empty reply segment no longer shifts every later reply onto the previous command's slot (misattributed values in the .par file / on the controller), and a short bulk reply pads the unanswered tail with the no-reply error filler instead of re-sending the boundary commands (a re-send could execute a parameter write twice). BulkCommandParser(index, response) now honors its documented 1-based contract: index 1 returns the first segment (previously the second), the last index returns the last segment (previously threw IndexOutOfRangeException), and out-of-range indexes return null. Tearing down one MotionController no longer harms the others in the process. A garbage-collected (undisposed) controller's finalizer called Shutdown() — which could take down the shared AACommServer — and its disconnect cleared the process-wide parameter-metadata cache under live sibling controllers, silently degrading their float parameter reads/writes to int handling until their next connect. The finalizer now only disconnects its own controller, Dispose() suppresses the finalizer, disconnect no longer clears the shared cache (each connect atomically rebuilds it), and only an explicit Shutdown() touches the server. The native aamotion SDK's Release/Disconnect likewise no longer shut the server down — the explicit Shutdown export is the only path that may. Enabling the fast-read cache no longer risks tearing down the connection when any call slower than ~200 ms is in flight — the background cache refresh used a hardcoded 100 ms timeout, tighter than any other command's wire budget; it now uses the default message timeout (a slow reply just delays the next refresh while readers serve the cached value). FastReadCache reads now honor validity: a registered-but-never-refreshed entry is a cache miss (falls back to a live read) instead of a fabricated 0, and a value whose refresh failed is not served stale. Disconnect invalidates all entries (no unbounded-stale values while no refresh can run) and the background refresh no-ops while disconnected instead of spamming an error event per interval — throttled to an idle poll (500 ms) so a 1 ms-interval cache no longer burns ~1000 no-op tasks per second while disconnected; it resumes the configured cadence by itself after a reconnect. FastReadCache.Dispose() no longer throws ObjectDisposedException on any cache that was ever used (its own disposed-guard fired mid-dispose) — on .NET Framework a garbage-collected undisposed cache could take the process down from the finalizer thread. UploadParameters() / DownloadParameters() summaries no longer count API-synthesized error replies (PC Suite: ERR …, BOOT … ERR, e.g. from a connection lost mid-transfer) as successes — error classification now matches the full AAComm reply taxonomy instead of only controller ERR … replies. Removed The C++/CLI AAMotionCPP (mixed-mode) and AGAAMotion (native shim) projects have been retired. Non-.NET (C/C++) consumers move to the new C-ABI SDK — aamotion.h + aamotion.dll/libaamotion.so/libaamotion.dylib (project AAMotionNative). The managed Agito.AAMotion API and the Java binding are unaffected. [10.0.0] - 2026-05-25 Added EnsureAACommServerRunning(): New method on IMotionController / MotionController that ensures the AACommServer is running and ready to accept connections. Launches the server if not already running, with proper path resolution. Deprecated AAMotionConfig.UseAsyncCommTransport: in AAComm 13.0.0 both flag values produce equivalent observable transport behavior for callers using a single path serially (false → CommAPI.SendReceive over the sync flow; true → CommAPI.Send + an internal wait-handle over the async flow — see issue #32 history). The flag is therefore a no-op for typical usage and will be removed in a future release. Changed DataLogger StartDataRecording: AGD155 and AGD155-EC now use ARecStart[1] command syntax (firmware v2.3+); other controllers continue to use ARecStart without index. Refactored DataLogger and SlowLogger to route all communication through CommAPIInterface.SendAndRecieve() instead of directly calling CommAPI.SendReceive(). This ensures consistent behavior when AAMotionConfig.UseAsyncCommTransport is enabled (async) or disabled (sync). [9.1.1] - 2026-04-17 Changed Packaging: picks up AAComm 12.1.1 sidecar change. AACommServer sidecar is now selected by consumer OS rather than TFM: Windows consumers (net48 or net8.0) get the WPF AACommServer.exe; non-Windows net8.0 consumers get AACommServerNetConsole. AAMotion consumers inherit this transitively — no code or reference changes required. [9.1.0] - 2026-04-15 Fixed ScanController / ScanControllerDetailed: Replaced unreliable TCP probe (TcpPortReachable) with ARP-based discovery via ARPTools.GetSubnetActiveIPs. This uses the same multi-NIC ARP scan as PCSuite's Discover Connections, ensuring controllers on all Ethernet interfaces are reliably found. [7.0.0] - 2024-12-30 ⚠️ Major Release Introduction of AAMotionAPI, a functional programming style API interface for users more familiar with C++ style programming. This interface is incomplete. AAMotion infrastructural level has been cleaned and redesigned: There are no more status updates. There are no more settings updates. There is a new type called AAValueArray which functions exactly like an array. All keywords are now accessible as a property. Some keywords are more like functions, in which case they are exposed via the API as methods. Hooking onto errors is now done via EventOccurred action in MotionController class. Documentations have currently all been removed, due to a large effort to clean the code base and remove code bloat, unify and to standardize the code style. Since there is now a direct link to keywords of the controller, it may be better to centralize efforts in documentations first. All design considerations are in an effort to speed up the performance of the API usage, as well as to simplify the overall design.
